MSI Prism SQL Inspector, Signing, .MST & .MSP

Enterprise deployment teams routinely inspect compiled Windows Installer tables, customize properties via Group Policy Transforms (.mst), distribute binary delta Patches (.msp), and verify dual-layer Authenticode digital signatures.

Inspecting Databases with RaggieSoft MSI Prism (msiprism.exe)

  • Opens any .msi (Installation Database), .msm (Merge Module), or .msp (Patch Package via MSIDBOPEN_PATCHFILE) in native 64-bit x64 and ARM64 Dark or Light Mode.
  • Displays all OLE SummaryInformation properties (including PID_TEMPLATE architecture/LCID and PID_REVNUMBER PackageCode) alongside every relational SQL table in _Tables.
  • Runs one-click ICE80 64-bit attribute and relational schema verification, and supports headless CI verification via msiprism.exe --inspect-summary <file>.

Dual-Layer Authenticode Code Signing

When [Signing] Enabled = true in your .rsip manifest (using either a local certificate store Thumbprint or Azure Artifact Signing DlibPath + MetadataJson), instbuild.exe signs in strict two-stage order:

  1. Signs the inner compiled Product.msi database first so Windows Installer's UAC prompt displays your verified publisher name.
  2. Compresses and embeds that signed Product.msi into Setup.exe via UpdateResourceW, then signs the outer Setup.exe executable!

Generating .MST Transforms & .MSP Patch Packages

Use View 9 (Signing, .MST & .MSP), the Release AeroWizard, or msiprism.exe to diff a baseline .msi against a customized or upgraded .msi and emit standard .mst Transforms (msiexec /i Product.msi TRANSFORMS=Org.mst /qn) or .msp Patch Packages.
